identity.title: Strategy Coopetition Explains the Emergence and Transience of In-Context Learning

problem.claim: The work seeks a mechanistic understanding of why emergent in-context learning can disappear after prolonged training.

contributions.claim: Introduces context-constrained in-weights learning (CIWL) as a hybrid asymptotic strategy and characterizes its competitive and cooperative interaction with ICL.
Proposes a minimal mathematical model that reproduces the reported strategy interactions and dynamics.
Identifies a setup reported to make ICL emergent and persistent.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors term the combined competitive and cooperative interaction between CIWL and ICL “strategy coopetition.”

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, after ICL disappears, CIWL becomes the dominant asymptotic strategy and replaces ICL.
In their setup, the authors report that ICL cannot emerge quickly independently and is enabled through the simultaneous slow development of CIWL.
The authors report that their mathematical model reproduces the key dynamics and interactions, and that it guided identification of a setup with persistent ICL.

narrative_sequence.summary: ICL is described as emergent and potentially transient, motivating a mechanistic investigation.
After ICL disappears, the model is reported to rely on hybrid CIWL, which competes with and replaces ICL.
Shared sub-circuits create cooperation as well as competition; CIWL can enable ICL’s emergence in the stated setup.
The authors name this interaction strategy coopetition, model it mathematically, and use the model to identify a persistent-ICL setup.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links ICL transience to a competing hybrid strategy while also reporting that the same strategy can help ICL emerge.

lessons.interpretation: A mechanism may have time-dependent effects that are jointly enabling and suppressive, so explanations should distinguish interaction phases.
lessons.application: Frame a learning-dynamics account by separately identifying each strategy’s early enabling role and late competitive replacement role.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the system has no identifiable competing strategies or temporal regime change.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, training setup, datasets, or measurements supporting the reported dynamics.
The conditions and operational criteria for ICL being “truly emergent and persistent” are not given.
The mathematical model’s assumptions, derivation, and quantitative agreement with experiments are unspecified.
